Apparatus criticus

  • Text from autopsy

translation

commentary

Orsi declined to speculate on the nature of the text in his original publication. Kaibel suggested that the fragment was part of a funerary verse epigram, a view which Manganaro merely repeated without reviewing the text in 1994. In 1999 instead, he suggested that this might be a fragment of an honorific text for a teacher of the youth of the gymnasium, and although his restorations are excessively speculative, the core points that we would seem to have the words καιρὸν, a form of the participle παιδευόμενος (the sequence of letters can hardly be restored as anything else), and a reference to ἀρετή, very strongly favour the suggestion. The vacats after lines 1 and 5 encourage the view that the right margin of the stone is preserved. The ΤΩΝ at the start of line 1 are perhaps more likely to be the end of a genitive plural, rather than the article, given the vacat. The survival of a high quality painted text from the Hellenistic period is unusual, but especially given the relatively poor quality of the local stone for epigraphic carving, perhaps should not be surprising.

Finely painted Hellenistic letters in rigid style without serfis. Alpha has straight bar; epsilon has short middle bar; omicron is small and above the line (14-17 mm); omega is small, circular, closed, and almost sits on the line (19 mm).
